# Our duty tool against duties actually assessed by Customs (generated by `python -m src.eval.gd_duty_compare`)

Source: an importer's Goods Declaration extract, Chapter 85, February 2026 (private; only anonymised results are kept). 1500 random home-consumption lines. Importer facts inferred per line (commercial importer if the 3% tax was charged; filer). Amounts compared within 2 rupees.

* Tool could compute: 1483 of 1500 lines. Others: needs_input 10, cannot_compute 7.

* **none**: 770 lines computed, 651 match on every tax (84%).
* **china_fta**: 524 lines computed, 120 match on every tax (22%).
* **fifth_schedule**: 45 lines computed, 1 match on every tax (2%).
* **sro_655_656**: 117 lines computed, 3 match on every tax (2%).
* **sales_tax_or_it_exemption**: 27 lines computed, 0 match on every tax (0%).

## Which tax differs (all computed lines)

| Tax | lines that differ | share |
|---|---|---|
| CD | 545 | 36.7% |
| RD | 24 | 1.6% |
| ACD | 182 | 12.3% |
| ST | 615 | 41.5% |
| VAT | 330 | 22.3% |
| IT | 685 | 46.2% |

Lines with no concession tag (plain rates) are the fair test of the duty rules. China FTA and Fifth Schedule lines show where concessions change the customs duty; the concessions work (docs/concessions_plan.md) should close those gaps.
